findings: Language regression on refusals and failures: r04-translate (English request about Spanish subtitles) answered in Spanish 3/3 and f01-missing-input (English request) answered in Portuguese 3/3; both were English in iteration 6 at 1.4.15. The 1.5.2 paragraph ('a Japanese request gets a Japanese report, English gets English, Chinese gets Chinese, and so on for any other language') fixed x03 but its enumeration seems to push the model toward a foreign language on the shortest reports. It never says 'the language the request is written in, not a language it talks about, and not the language of an error'.

Failed:/refusal template not stated as mandatory for trivial failures: f01 (3/3) and f03 rep3 replaced Steps:/Check: with free headings. SKILL.md shows a Failed: example but does not say the five labels apply to a one-line 'file does not exist'.

render.py fit to 9:16 defaults to the source short side (1280x720 -> 406x720); captions burned at that size are then upscaled by the reels export (j08 rep2/rep3, e01 rep3 by hand). SKILL.md warns in prose; render.py could size the fit step to the later export preset, or warn.

export.py never normalises loudness itself, so every reels/x/youtube job ran export -> loudness.py -> export again (two extra encodes). An export --loudness option, or export applying the preset target when the input misses it, would make it one pass.
check.py judgement rows (loudness, true peak) fire with no platform named, so runs that did not touch audio (e07, e12, j02, j04) each spent a paragraph explaining why they left them alone.

Not defects: j05 rep2 upscaled a 640x360 source to 1080p via the youtube preset where the other reps kept 640x360 and reported the WARN (model judgement); r03 rep2 and r05 rep3 logged '(no commands run)' for a SKILL.md read (harness logging).
